text: True or False: A perfectly matched layer (PML) is an artificial absorber that terminates a finite simulation grid as if it opened onto infinite space, preventing spurious reflections off the domain boundary.
explanation: True — Berenger's PML absorbs outgoing radiation with reflections below -60 dB when properly graded, so a finite grid mimics open space. Without it, boundary reflections corrupt any radiating or scattering simulation; a misconfigured (too thin or too abrupt) PML is a leading source of spurious artifacts.
